Criterion: Verify that exits are lockable, simple to open, and do not open in flight unless mission requirements necessitate this function. Standard (Air Force): All exits are lockable by aircrew trained to do so. All exits are uncomplicated to open such that no training is required for operation. All exits will stay locked and closed in passenger compartments when the aircraft is inflight unless mission needs allow the opening and use of exits inflight. Method of Compliance (Air Force): Analysis, demonstration and inspection documentation verifies that all exits in passenger areas are lockable by aircrew, simple to open without training, and will stay locked in flight when not opened for mission need. Human factors analysis and demonstration verify the expected passenger population's abilities to operate exits. References: JSSG-2010-7: 3.7.5.3.1 14 CFR 25.813, 25.809, 23.807, 25.813

Standard: All exits are lockable by a crewmember trained to do so. All exits are uncomplicated to open so that no training is required for operation. All exits stay locked and closed in compartments when the air vehicle is inflight unless mission needs allow the opening and use of exits in flight. The design of all exits provide clear indication that the doors are fully locked in flight. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of engineering drawings or digital models verifies that there is clear indication of a locked or unlocked condition.
(2) Examination of the physical air vehicle configuration verifies that there is clear indication of a locked or unlocked condition. Demonstration.
  (1) Trained crewmembers demonstrate that exits are lockable, simple to open, and stay locked in flight when not opened for mission needs.
